exclusion_groups.why: CustomTalk menu label: ●妖怪メダル交換(たぶん翻訳不要) — "Yo-kai medal exchange (probably no translation needed)". The parenthetical is the localiser's own note, left in the string and identical in all three columns, so this is the rare case where the row SAYS it is a leaving. Its two neighbours in the same sheet — ●ここの天気は？ and ●鑑定する — are NOT excluded and are translated: they are ordinary Japanese that English never localised, which is a different class entirely and one the spec is explicit about.

●イースター：00924_01：ラニエット — "Easter : 00924_01 : Laniette". This one HAS the colons and an id, so it looks like the pattern's own shape, and it still escapes: AssetIdToken requires a letter-led token and 00924_01 is all digits. Widening that regex to accept a bare numeric run would start matching real dialogue that quotes a number, so the row comes here instead.

PublicContentTextData: an Odin fight's TIMELINE. These say WHEN a line plays, not what is said. Note the three gaps: #2110, #2111 and #2113 sit inside the range and ARE real barks, which is exactly why this is a list and not a range.

exclusion_groups.why: The 13 LogMessage rows whose English column is Japanese, listed 12 August 2026. They are a hand list and not a regex ON PURPOSE: the markers here are 予備 («spare»), （仮） («provisional») and 削除 («deleted»), and PlaceholderJapanese is also run against the ja and fr columns of every row in the corpus, so teaching it those three characters would start deleting real Japanese prose that happens to contain them. Two of these say outright what they are — （※予備。翻訳不要）, «spare, no translation needed».  NOT every Japanese-looking LogMessage row: the 17 others in this sheet whose English renders as « .» are the delivery and summoning messages, real text hidden inside a branch, and they stay in and are translated from the French.

exclusion_groups.why: TstPlnCmpFCCounter_00035 and TstPrgTest_00001, 68 rows: the game's own test scaffolding, left in the sheets. Tst is the file-name prefix for it exactly as Cmn and Reg are for real content, and it is a CLOSED SET — those two conversations and no others. Their English column is Japanese throughout, and TstPrgTest says what it is: シナリオテキストテスト１, «scenario text test 1», followed by シナリオテキストテスト2sdfsd, which is a hand resting on the keyboard. Listed by key and not by prefix, because a prefix rule is the kind that deletes real dialogue the day someone ships a quest that happens to start with those three letters.
The remaining four せーりーふー rows — «diaaalogue», a slot marker with nothing in it. The fifth went out with the svc-02 batch.

exclusion_groups.why: RegFstHowToAutoAttack_00027, all 14 rows: a CustomTalk widget test left in the sheets. The English column is Japanese and says so outright — «カスタムトークテストです。このページ以降、 ウィジェットの可変テストになります。», «this is a CustomTalk test; from this page on it is a widget variability test» — and the French and Japanese columns are the same characters. Found by the svc-04 translator, who reported them rather than inventing Spanish for a test page.

EVERY ROW A REALM REBORN HAD LEFT, 12 August 2026, read in all three languages first. The block sat at 99% with these 57 as the whole remainder, and not one of them is a line: the French and Japanese say so outright — 空 (empty), 空ラベル (empty label), 削除ラベル (deleted label), （カット）, （削除）, 待機＆討伐仮 («wait and kill, provisional») — or they hold the designer's own working note, complete with `pop`, `eobj` and raw <sheet(BNpcName,…)> ids, while the English column carries its `//:` summary of the same note.  GaiUsa908_00803 is the one to look at twice: its French reads as ordinary French («Inspecter 3 constructions endommagées») because the French team translated the note. The English is still «//: inspect scaffolding, kill monster» and the Japanese is still a note, which is the same shape as ClsTan005_00051 above and settles it the same way.
